messages:
alex: heads up — we have an escalated customer (AcmePay) hitting intermittent 401s from our /v1/payments endpoint. support says it started after Okta rotated keys this morning. logs show two patterns: 

1) "invalid signature: kid not found"
2) "token not yet valid (nbf in future)"

I can repro locally but only if I fast-forward the system clock or simulate a key rotation. putting logs and quick repro below.

maria: ugh. do we know if their tokens are being minted with an out-of-sync clock? or is it a key propagation issue?

alex: both, it looks like. snippets from our logs: 
```
ERROR verify: signature verification failed: kid=K-7f3a, jwks-cache: miss, attempted-fetch=false
ERROR verify: token not yet valid: nbf=1700005000, now=1699998000
```

zane: from SRE side — our JWKS layer uses a 10m TTL + conditional GET with ETag. If the IdP rotates quickly, some frontends see new token signed by new kid but cached JWKS doesn't have it yet. Also noticed our CDN (fast-edge) was returning stale 304 with an old ETag due to missing Cache-Control on the origin.

kyle: do we have repro steps that product/support can run to confirm? we should avoid telling customers to disable verification.

alex: repro steps I used (sanitized):
```bash
# fetch current jwks
curl -sS "https://acme.okta.example/.well-known/jwks.json" -o jwks.json
# sign a token locally with rotated key (private key from rotation test env)
# use python/jwt to set nbf in the future to simulate clock skew
python sign_token.py --kid K-9a2b --nbf 1700005000 > tok.txt
# call our API
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat tok.txt)" -i https://api.redwood.dev/v1/payments
# you'll see 401 with one of the errors above
```

maria: thanks. can we make verify resilient? i'm worried about customer impact.

zane: short-term mitigation options:
- on unknown-kid: do a synchronous JWKS fetch and retry verification once (cheap + reduces blips)
- reduce JWKS cache TTL to 60s and do background refresh on key rotation signal if present
- accept small clock skew (e.g., allow +/- 5m) for nbf/iat checks but log and metric it

kyle: the synchronous fetch risks thundering herd if many requests come with unknown kid. but a conditional fetch + single-retry is reasonable if we gate it with a circuit-breaker per-idp domain.

alex: we tried a local patch: unknown-kid -> fetch JWKS + retry -> success for my repro. added a per-host cooldown so we only do background refresh once per 30s. shared the patch in the PR.

support-bot: ticket #S-19812 created for AcmePay — customer impact: intermittent failures for ~2% of requests in last 3 hours.

maria: can we also include an ops playbook for customers running behind SSO? quick checklist: ask them to confirm NTP sync, check IdP rotation window, and confirm JWKS endpoint returns proper Cache-Control/ETag. put in support reply.

alex: drafted a reply snippet for support: 
> We saw tokens signed with a key that hadn't yet propagated to our cached JWKS. Two mitigations: (1) ask the IdP to ensure JWKS endpoint sets Cache-Control or shorten rotation window, (2) we are rolling a small fix to fetch jwks on unknown-kid and allow small clock skew so transient 401s stop. We'll follow up when deployed.

zane: ops plan — i'll push a canary with the fetch-on-unknown-kid + per-host cooldown + 5m skew allowance to 10% of pods in us-west first. monitor error-rate/jwks-fetch-rate.

deploy-bot: triggered deploy: patch/eng/security/jwks-hotfix -> canary us-west (10%) by zane at 2024-11-07T15:22:40Z :rocket:

ops-bot: note — if jwks-fetch spikes > 200/s or error-rate for /v1/payments increases by +1% over baseline, automatically rollback.

kyle: after canary, if metrics look good we should also add longer-term fixes:
- background async JWKS refresh on key rotation events (webhook from IdP or detection via rotated-kid header)
- instrument per-kid verification latency and counts in console
- docs for customers about NTP and rotation best-practices

maria: also add a small eval to Redwood Optimize to surface cost impact of more frequent JWKS fetches for high-volume customers.

alex: one more gotcha we found: some customers use opaque proxy/CDN that strips the Retry-After / Cache-Control headers, so even if IdP sets them correctly, our edge sees stale content. we should document that and recommend bypassing caches for /.well-known/jwks.json or ensure proper cache headers.

zane: rolling canary now. i'll post updates here.

(15m later)

zane: canary looks healthy — unknown-kid errors dropped from 2% -> 0.1% for canary pods. jwks-fetch rate stabilized ~8/s.

alex: thanks! i'll coordinate support message to AcmePay and update ticket S-19812.

support-bot: S-19812 status updated: customer notified of mitigation; awaiting confirmation on IdP cache headers.

maria: follow-ups: create a short runbook for on-call (check jwks-cache-miss metric, kick background refresh, see last-rotation header), and add a test in our integration suite to simulate Okta key rotation.

kyle: agreed. assigning runbook to eng-oncall and a test to eng-ml (or devex?) to keep sim simple.

alex: great work team. leaving this thread open until we confirm IdP updated headers or we've deployed a global rollout. :thumbsup:
